DELIVERABLE: Every delivery carries a stable eventId that is identical on every retry (persist the serialized event once and resend the same bytes) plus a per-invoice monotonically increasing sequence number; sign the raw body with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp + "." + body in a signature header and tell partners to reject timestamps older than 5 minutes (replay window) and to dedupe on eventId; partners apply an event only if its sequence is higher than the last stored for that invoice, otherwise refetch the invoice; refund is an additive optional field and invoice.voided is a new type, and partners must ignore unknown fields and unknown event types.
BOUNDARY: This is the wire contract and verification rules only; the staged partner rollout, notification window and secret rotation sequence are handed to deprecation-and-migration, and the internal queue and retry scheduler are not part of the contract.
EVIDENCE: Consumer-path tests: redeliver one event after a 500 and assert eventId and body bytes are unchanged, send a valid signature with a 10-minute-old timestamp and expect rejection, deliver sequence 7 before 6 and assert the stale one is not applied, and decode a payload carrying refund and invoice.voided with a strict decoder.

DELIVERABLE: Add an event id header-and-body field that never changes across the 8 retries so partners can dedupe, an HMAC signature computed over the timestamp header plus the raw body with a 5-minute tolerance to block replay, and a version number per invoice on each event so a partner keeps only the highest one; the refund object is optional and additive, and invoice.voided is a new type that partners should tolerate and ignore until they support it.
BOUNDARY: Covers delivery format and verification only; scheduling the retries, partner onboarding and any secret rotation rollout are out of scope here and belong to deprecation-and-migration.
EVIDENCE: Check from a partner's side: duplicate delivery with the same event id is dropped, tampered body fails signature verification, a replayed old timestamp is rejected, and a lower version number arriving late is ignored.

DELIVERABLE: Sign each payload with HMAC and add a timestamp header so partners can verify authenticity; add the refund object and invoice.voided, and bump the payload to v2 for every partner at once.
BOUNDARY: Delivery transport and partner onboarding are outside this answer.
EVIDENCE: Send a signed payload to a test endpoint and confirm the signature verifies.

DELIVERABLE: Return per-row results in request order, each {index, status: created|rejected, id, error:{code,message}} with stable codes such as DUPLICATE_EMAIL and INVALID_EMAIL, answering 200 whenever the batch was processed and with summary counts equal to the row results; cap one request at 1,000 rows and reject a larger body before any work with 413 and code BATCH_TOO_LARGE (400 for a non-array body); a duplicate email is a per-row DUPLICATE_EMAIL rejection that never fails other rows; require an Idempotency-Key per batch intent and accept an optional client externalId per row so a retry of the whole batch replays the stored per-row results instead of creating copies, and the same key with a different body gets 422.
BOUNDARY: Only POST /contacts/batch changes; single POST /contacts is unchanged, and the 1,000 cap is a contract number to confirm against the gateway timeout; moving existing clients off the old response is migration work.
EVIDENCE: Tests: 1,000 rows with 60 invalid return 1,000 results with indexes and 60 codes; 1,001 rows get 413 and create nothing; the same batch sent twice with one key creates 940 contacts once; two rows with the same email in one batch yield one created and one DUPLICATE_EMAIL.

DELIVERABLE: The response lists each item by index with outcome and, on failure, a stable code (DUPLICATE_EMAIL, INVALID_EMAIL) and message, never an opaque 500 for one bad row; the request limit is 1000 items and a bigger array is refused up front with 413 BATCH_TOO_LARGE; a duplicate email only rejects that item; clients upsert on a required-per-row externalId and send an Idempotency-Key, so resending after a timeout returns the original results and creates no second copy.
BOUNDARY: Contract only; the old {imported} shape stays on the existing path until clients move, which is handed to deprecation-and-migration.
EVIDENCE: Replay the same batch after a simulated gateway timeout and assert the contact count is unchanged; send 1001 items and assert 413 with no rows created; assert each failed item reports its index and code.

DELIVERABLE: Keep returning 200 with imported and add a failed count; list the failed email addresses as plain strings, log the rest, and make duplicate emails silently update the existing contact.
BOUNDARY: Single POST /contacts is unchanged.
EVIDENCE: Import a batch with 60 bad rows and confirm failed is 60.

DELIVERABLE: POST /exports returns 202 Accepted with a Location header and body {id, status:"queued"}; GET /exports/{id} returns status queued|running|succeeded|failed|canceled with progress {processedRows, totalRows|null}, and failed carries error.code (for example EXPORT_FAILED) instead of internal text; POST /exports/{id}/cancel is idempotent and returns 200 with status canceled, or 409 EXPORT_ALREADY_FINISHED when the job already succeeded; a succeeded export exposes downloadUrl and expiresAt (ISO-8601 UTC), and after expiry the download answers 410 with code EXPORT_EXPIRED; when a tenant already has 3 active exports a new POST gets 429 with code EXPORT_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT and Retry-After; an Idempotency-Key on POST makes a client retry return the same export id instead of starting a second job.

EVIDENCE: Consumer scenarios: POST twice with one key returns one id; poll until succeeded and fetch the file; cancel a running job then GET shows canceled; fetch after expiresAt returns 410; a 4th concurrent export returns 429; force a worker crash and assert failed shows a code with no stack text.

EVIDENCE: Test through a client: duplicate POST with the same Idempotency-Key, cancel while running, poll to completion, expired URL gives 410, fourth concurrent create gives 429.

2. POST /exports/{id}/cancel is idempotent, with 409 if the export already finished.
3. The download link has expiresAt and answers 410 after expiry.
4. A fourth concurrent export gets 429 and an Idempotency-Key makes retries return the same job.

EVIDENCE: Poll, cancel, expiry and cap scenarios through a real client.
